regime.note: The Federal Reserve publishes September 15–16 minutes on October 7 and meets October 27–28. Low confidence and 64% cash reflect near-term policy risk, extended screen leaders, and the analyst book’s worsening negative alpha.

thesis: Hold the September 29 event-driven reset for one more settled session. VRTX and NEM remain pre-event positions rather than tape-following trades: Vertex’s November 30 povetacicept PDUFA is the core binary catalyst, while Newmont’s confirmed October 22 results are 12 trading sessions away. The October 5 whole-universe screen remains crowded: SOXL and MRNA gained about 40% over 20 sessions, AMD 32%, DDOG 30%, NET 29%, and CRWD 28%; most leaders carry RSI readings above 70 or premium/negative earnings multiples. Robinhood fundamentals show VRTX at 29.292841x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.625030x, while the paper book trails SPY by 18.6 points with a -3.68 Sharpe. No new momentum exposure is justified; retain 64% cash, lower confidence to 0.34, and keep weights capped. This is the project’s paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists September 15–16 meeting minutes for October 7 and the next FOMC meeting for October 27–28, with a press conference on October 28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; RAINIER showed a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and a 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001).
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood’s October 6 data shows VRTX at 29.292841x P/E, $127.13 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.8889 mean analyst target.
Robinhood’s October 6 data shows NEM at 14.625030x P/E, $120.89 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $140.1171 mean analyst target.
At the October 5 settled close, VRTX was $503.50 and NEM $115.82; VRTX fell 0.24% while NEM rose 0.22% from October 2.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
NEM remains 9.2% below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 64% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The portfolio has produced -18.6 points of all-time alpha with a -3.68 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

reflection.looking_back: The marked book is down 16.0% versus SPY up 2.6%, or -18.6 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.68 annualized 37-session Sharpe. Over the latest settled session the book was flat while SPY gained 0.7%, a 0.7-point alpha miss; VRTX is 3.6% below entry and NEM 9.2% below entry.
worked: VRTX and NEM still have company-confirmed future checkpoints, keeping both theses falsifiable rather than dependent on undated momentum.
The 64% cash buffer avoided adding to a screen dominated by 20-session gains of roughly 28%–40%.
missed: The book lost another 0.7 point of alpha on October 5, so neither event sleeve has earned higher confidence.
VRTX declined 0.24% and NEM rose only 0.22% on October 5; pre-catalyst drift remains too weak to justify adding.
reflection.adjustment: Lower confidence from 0.35 to 0.34, keep VRTX at 20% and NEM at 16%, retain 64% cash, and continue refusing to chase extended semiconductor/software/biotech screen leaders.
